executiveSummary: GM0405 is identity-correct, deterministic and numerically complete across ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services, but is not a calibrated Hoorn first-72-hour forecast. Official local evidence identifies Visserseiland, Oostereiland and Julianapark as outer-dike areas and records 2023–2024 Markermeer nuisance at Visserseiland and Grashaven around NAP +20 cm; the canonical coastal preset instead assigns a broad 1.519909 legacy flood amplitude and 53,481 affected people-equivalent at T+24 without a selected lake level, wind setup, defence or breach state. Seven unrelated non-compound hazards reuse the same top-five neighbourhood order, while the four Binnenstad neighbourhoods rank 9th, 27th, 47th and 56th under coastal forcing. Public dike, water-asset, road, grid, telecom, education and acute-care sources add strong context but not live capacity or restoration. Unsupported direct flood and neighbourhood precision must be suppressed or replaced; missing operational state remains Unknown, never zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0405 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and neighbourhoods
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS data identify GM0405 as Hoorn and report 76,036 residents, density 3,732 per square kilometre, 20.9% aged 65 or older and 13,413 one-person households. Rounded, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable neighbourhood fields retain distinct null/zero semantics.

The municipal reference point [5.065163480473221, 52.655726179359135] lies inside the 2025 generalized multipolygon. BAG provides Blokker, Hoorn and Zwaag under Public Domain Mark 1.0; the Hoorn woonplaats label point lies outside the independently generalized CBS boundary, a reproducible generalization/centroid caveat rather than proof that the place is misassigned.

The 74 published neighbourhood populations sum to 76,035, one below the municipal total (-0.001%); allocation reconciles exactly to 76,036. Registers do not measure event-time tourists, harbour users, commuters, hospital occupants, home-care dependency or household supplies.

evidenceSources.title: NWB, rail and scheduled public-transport inputs for Hoorn
evidenceSources.edition: NWB 1 August 2026; ProRail/OVapi snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates three logical boundary links: A7 south to Koggenland, A7 north to Medemblik and N307 to Medemblik. The two A7 links are series segments of one physical corridor; generalized 260/150 capacities are non-additive scenario ceilings, not measured traffic or emergency throughput.

ProRail's CC0 OGC service locates Hoorn and Hoorn Kersenboogerd stations; GTFS preprocessing finds 95 stop areas, including Dijklander Ziekenhuis. Geometry and schedules do not establish event-time operation, evacuation throughput, hospital access, fuel, staffing or restoration.
No current NDW record in the bounded deployment snapshot is assigned to GM0405. That is partial time/coverage output and cannot be interpreted as every road being open.

evidenceSources.title: Beleidsplan Veiligheidsregio Noord-Holland Noord 2024–2027 and public crisis organisation
evidenceSources.edition: Policy plan adopted 15 March 2024; public risk-profile link remains 2022–2024 pending newer accessible product
supports: The adopted policy framework prioritizes preparation for extreme weather including flooding and for electricity outage, and describes collaboration with Hoogheemraadschap Hollands Noorderkwartier. The public organisation page lists HHNK, hospitals, GGD, police, KNRM, Red Cross and Defence as partners.

The public crisis page at https://www.vrnhn.nl/ons-werk/crisisbeheersing says the generic organisation scales flexibly to incident need and distinguishes crisis teams, mayor and population care. These governance statements do not prove that a GM0405 action, resource, facility or restoration step is assigned or completed.
Regional documents are planning/governance evidence without municipality-specific numeric impact curves, machine event state or a stated blanket reuse licence.

evidenceSources.title: Buitendijkse gebieden en hoogwater, sewer renewal, storm response and 72-hour preparedness
supports: Hoorn identifies Visserseiland, Oostereiland and Julianapark as outer-dike areas. High Markermeer levels caused nuisance at Visserseiland and Grashaven in late 2023/early 2024; new safety-region notification arrangements use expected NAP +20 cm as an operational attention threshold. The municipality added sewer isolation at Visserseiland and raised electrical points/manhole covers at Grashaven. These are specific context and measures, not a future flood footprint or guaranteed protection.

The municipality assigns Markermeer level management to Rijkswaterstaat, dike/land-behind safety to HHNK, and safety assessment/measures during emergency to municipality plus safety region. The simulator must preserve those authorities rather than infer a generic coastal response.

Official sewer pages say the Binnenstad, part of Grote Waal, old Blokker and old Zwaag have mixed sewers and that a cloudburst can exceed them. Hoorn-Noord/Venenlaankwartier renewal separates rainwater, adds drainage and runs in phases through 2027. Local projects do not establish municipality-wide live drainage capacity.

The 72-hour page at https://www.hoorn.nl/denkvooruit/We-moeten-72-uur-zelfredzaam-zijn-Wat-houdt-dat-in.html says power, water and full shop shelves may be unavailable and emergency services cannot be everywhere at once. It expressly says an incident may last longer than 72 hours; guidance is not measured preparedness, guaranteed aid or recovery.

evidenceSources.title: Markermeer defences, outer-dike exposure, IJsselmeergebied water management and official water data routes
evidenceSources.edition: Current pages and machine snapshots inspected 3 September 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: HHNK says almost all Hollands Noorderkwartier lies below sea level and primary defences protect against Markermeer/IJsselmeer/North Sea/Wadden Sea, while areas outside them can flood under exceptional conditions. The 33-km Markermeerdijk Hoorn–Durgerdam strengthening is continuing; project need/status is not a breach, all-clear or event-time defence condition.

Rijkswaterstaat explains at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/water/vaarwegenoverzicht/ijsselmeer/waterbeheer-ijsselmeer-markermeer that Markermeer level depends on river inflow, rainfall, wind setup and discharge through the Houtrib/Afsluitdijk system. Its Waterbericht is hourly automatic guidance looking at most 48 hours ahead, not a synthetic T+72 forecast.

LIWO release 2025.1.6 at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows is an irregular expert scenario library. A defensible run must retain scenario/release, source water body, boundary hydrograph/level, datum, wind, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession, probability, resolution, layer licence, coverage and NoData; LIWO is not live observation.

The deployed CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH services contain 90 GM0405 point assets: 38 sewer pumps, 19 surface-water pumps and 33 weirs; 52 name HHNK, 38 have no manager and 56 have non-null capacity. Contributor completeness varies, and points/capacities do not prove units, topology, operation, backup or spare capacity. No Waterinfo observation or forecast is assigned locally; absence is coverage, not normal/safe water.

evidenceSources.publisher: Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: Public provider territories, grid-planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Provider/register/planning snapshots retrieved in 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1
supports: The Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting WMS identifies Liander electricity/gas, PWN drinking water and Ziggo media at the municipal reference point; provider dates range from September 2025 to March 2026 and drainage returns empty. A single-point territory result is not municipality-wide completeness, topology, outage, quality, capacity or restoration.

The single sampled Liander station OS HOORN HOLENWEG 10-1i reports withdrawal 20 MW existing/27 required plus 6.9 MW across 26 queued requests, injection 36/19 MW plus 26 MW queued, and 33 projects earliest 2026. NBNL planning is at least quarterly and queues monthly; its exact dataset licence was not found. It is not current load, household availability, reserve or T+72 state.

RDI WFS returns 114 antenna sites, including 38 mobile and 25 fixed-link sites; no fixed refresh or reuse licence was stated. Daily DUO RIO under CC BY (version unspecified) returns 56 education records. These do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, shelter role, occupancy, staff, supplies or live status.

RIVM acute-care questionnaire v1.1, published 3 July 2026 under CC0, identifies Dijklander Ziekenhuis Hoorn as 24/7 SEH plus acute obstetrics with 15 reported rooms and 21,650 2025 visits. The annual questionnaire is not live acceptance, occupancy, staffing, generator/fuel endurance or incident capacity.

evidenceSources.title: Spoedeisende Hulp Hoorn and access information
supports: The hospital states that Hoorn has 24/7 paediatrics, anaesthesia and operating team availability and treats most trauma, while serious brain/chest trauma generally transfers to Amsterdam UMC. This establishes service role and cross-boundary dependency, not disaster-time acceptance or capacity.

The route page at https://www.dijklander.nl/praktische-informatie/route-en-parkeren/route-en-parkeren-hoorn places the hospital near Hoorn station and A7 exit 8. Road/rail proximity does not prove access during flood, storm, outage or cyber disruption.
No public machine feed for live diversion, beds, staff, critical utilities, backup duration, oxygen, medicines or restoration was identified. Those states remain Unknown unless operator-authorized.

identity.summary: Official code, name, province, safety region, centre and headline demography agree.
notes: GM0405 is uniquely Hoorn in Noord-Holland and Veiligheidsregio Noord-Holland-Noord.
Boundary/statistics editions are 2025; present observations, project dates, annual registers and the synthetic exercise clock stay separate.
The municipality reference point is contained and no headline mismatch was found.

geography.summary: Municipal geometry is coherent, but BAG label generalization and lake/defence/drainage mechanisms require explicit source geometry.
notes: The BAG Hoorn label point lies outside the independently generalized municipal boundary while Blokker and Zwaag centres are contained; this is flagged rather than silently moved.

Official local evidence distinguishes protected interior from Visserseiland, Oostereiland and Julianapark outside the dike. A shoreline-distance field cannot replace the primary defence, outer-dike, sewer and lake-level geometries.
Every LIWO/HWH/municipal layer needs its own version, scenario, coverage, resolution, licence and NoData mask.

demography.summary: Official 2025 totals agree and neighbourhood rounding reconciles exactly.
notes: Population 76,036, density 3,732, age65Pct 20.9 and one-person households 13,413 agree.
Neighbourhood population sums to 76,035, one below the total; generated allocation reconciles to 76,036. Published households sum to 35,040 and age65+ rows to 15,885.
Largest neighbourhood is Kersenboogerd-Zuid Buurt 33 06 at 4,185; register counts omit visitors, harbour users and Dijklander occupancy.

regionalDetail.summary: All 74 neighbourhoods load, but several official fields and all operational states are incomplete.
notes: District heat and charging are missing for 74/74; home value/housing/tenure for eight; household size for three; cars per household for thirteen; benefit fields for nine; doctor/supermarket distance and density for six. Null is not zero.
HWH supplies 90 context points but 34 capacities are null and 38 managers are Unknown; non-null values are not comparable throughput without units/connectivity/state.
Provider, planning, antenna, education and acute-care records do not establish event-time availability.

settlements.summary: Blokker, Hoorn and Zwaag are the coherent settlement set, with one documented label-point/generalization caveat.
notes: BAG and BRT both yield the three woonkernen; the Hoorn label point falls outside only the independent generalized boundary test.
Do not snap or discard the label without comparing source-resolution geometries and editions.
Settlement labels cannot establish transient population, evacuation demand, reception or supply role.

transport.summary: A7/N307 and rail are reproducible, but internal crossings, hospital access and event-time passability remain unresolved.
notes: Three logical edges connect only Koggenland and Medemblik; A7 series links are non-additive.
NWB correctly transfers only mobility and road-logistics supply, never utilities/facilities.
Two stations and 95 stops provide schedule context; Dijklander depends on local/A7/rail access but current acceptance and routes are Unknown.
Empty bounded NDW output is not an all-open assertion.

emergencyContext.summary: Authorities, 72-hour guidance and a hospital role are identified, but no auditable local action/resource state exists.
notes: Hoorn documents a high-water notification threshold and distinct RWS/HHNK/municipality/safety-region roles; none is represented as trigger, authority, assignment, resource, status or completion.
Dijklander is a critical local and regional acute-care dependency, not guaranteed capacity. Serious trauma transfer, access, power, water, telecom, oxygen and staff remain Unknown.

Required action categories include warning, outer-dike welfare/evacuation, defence/sewer decisions, roads/rail, hospital continuity, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repair and mutual aid.
Household 72-hour guidance is not measured stock or a recovery deadline.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten presets return complete finite deterministic results at all six checkpoints and eight services; realism failures are separate.
notes: Mandatory and focused gates covered ten presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.

Outputs are synthetic exercise indices; affected people-equivalent is not observed people/casualties and person-hours is cumulative weighted local pre-network service shortfall versus a matched baseline.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, zero-event baseline, reconciliation and monotonic burden contracts pass.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0405 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across the complete matrix.
Intensity-zero event effects are zero, repeat runs and UI/core presets agree, and local allocation reconciles exactly.
Service-layer selection preserves physical hazard, route ceilings hold and event-attributable person-hours is monotonic.
Arithmetic correctness does not establish local calibration.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Broad coastal impact and a repeated neighbourhood ordering contradict source-specific local pathways.
notes: Coastal T+24 applies 1.519909 legacy flood amplitude and affects 53,481 people-equivalent without Markermeer level, wind setup, primary-defence/breach or outer-dike footprint.
The four Binnenstad neighbourhoods rank only 9th, 27th, 47th and 56th, while official exposure names Visserseiland, Oostereiland, Julianapark and Grashaven.

Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share the same T+24 top five: Hoorn Noord 12 04, Venelaankwartier 11 00, Grote Waal 13 02, Blokker 31 04 and Risdam-Noord 21 04. Compound saturates differently; river/earthquake are zero ties.
Canonical wildfire has zero direct fire but synthetic smoke/drought; it cannot validate a local fire footprint.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service percentages are inspectable but not calibrated to Hoorn utilities, drainage, transport or Dijklander.
notes: Coastal T+24 availability is power 32.34%, water 43.44%, drainage 21.33%, gas 66.49%, telecom 32.09%, mobility 30.27%, facilities 33.92%, supply 31.81%; no operator validates these values.
Liander/PWN/Ziggo territory, one NBNL sample, HWH assets and RDI sites remain non-causal context.
Hospital registration and public opening do not establish its power/water/telecom/oxygen/staff dependencies or incident acceptance.
Sensitive or unavailable topology must use explicit aggregate synthetic fallback, not invented public precision.

causalTrace.summary: Evidence classes are present but unresolved lake, defence, target and operational dimensions are not declared.
notes: Coastal reports derived-screening with unsupportedDimensions=[] despite no named Markermeer event, water level/datum, wind setup, defence/breach state, footprint or arrival/recession.
A legacy field named floodDepthM must not be presented as surveyed metres.
Current/project/register sources and synthetic T+72 have different valid times and cannot be fused.
Cyber needs an explicit target; empty observations/providers must become Unknown, not inferred normality.

recovery72h.summary: Coastal and compound residual impacts are deterministic but unsupported by local water, operator, hospital or action evidence.
notes: Coastal direct severity/flood amplitude returns to zero by T+72, yet pressure is 0.296279, affected people-equivalent 16,742 and person-hours 2,796,960.33. Availability remains power 0.649468, water 0.770177, drainage 0.572776, gas 0.852560, telecom 0.664585, mobility 0.724929, facilities 0.706744 and supply 0.692096.
Compound T+72 severity/pressure/affected/person-hours is 0.596935/0.662413/55,964/3,130,079.19; all eight availability values remain exactly at the T+24 plateau.
No lake recession/dewatering, sewer operation, defence decision, utility repair, route reopening, hospital acceptance, household stock or confirmed intervention supports those curves.
Seventy-two hours is a preparedness horizon; the source itself says emergencies can last longer.

findings.summary: The coastal preset overgeneralizes a Markermeer/defence problem into unsupported citywide direct flooding.
findings.evidence: Official Hoorn evidence names three outer-dike areas and a 2023–2024 nuisance event at Visserseiland/Grashaven around NAP +20 cm. The model instead reports legacy flood amplitude 1.519909 and 53,481 affected people-equivalent at T+24 with no level, wind setup, defence/breach or footprint.
findings.action: Suppress direct coastal impact outside a supported named Markermeer/outer-dike or LIWO defence scenario. Add lake level/datum, wind, defence state, footprint, arrival/recession, version, licence, coverage and NoData; distinguish lake flooding from North Sea coastal surge.

findings.summary: Neighbourhood ranking is not derived from outer-dike, drainage, heat or hazard-specific geometry.
findings.evidence: Seven unrelated non-compound hazards reuse one top-five order. Under coastal forcing Binnenstad neighbourhoods rank 9/27/47/56 despite official waterfront exposure being concentrated around Visserseiland, Oostereiland, Julianapark and Grashaven.
findings.action: Remove the shared local multiplier from physical hazard rank. Render unresolved municipal amplitude uniformly or Unknown until per-hazard source surfaces are integrated; test the named exposed polygons and hazard rank diversity.

findings.summary: Pluvial depth and impact precision lacks sewer/topographic calibration.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports legacy flood amplitude 0.696462 and 27,468 affected people-equivalent. Municipal sources identify mixed sewers and phased renewals in specific districts, but no rainfall event, surface model, inlet capacity, groundwater or live drainage state drives the output.
findings.action: Integrate municipality/HHNK stress-test or 3Di output with rainfall hyetograph, AHN/BGT, sewer-included flag, groundwater/saturation, resolution, edition/licence and NoData; otherwise label local depth/affected count unsupported.

findings.summary: Exact utility and restoration percentages have no operator evidence.
findings.evidence: Eight precise coastal availability values are produced from generic dependencies; public Liander/PWN/Ziggo territories, NBNL planning, HWH and RDI records provide no outage, topology, backup, switching or repair state.
findings.action: Keep public context affectsSimulation=false and label operational values aggregate synthetic/Unknown. Accept only authorized time-scoped operator aggregates and retain manual incident override provenance.

findings.summary: Water-control points are valuable context but incomplete and non-operational.
findings.evidence: Ninety HWH points are present; 38 lack manager and 34 lack capacity. Values cannot be summed as system capacity without units, connectivity and state; no local Waterinfo observation/forecast is assigned.
findings.action: Retain points, managers, nulls, source collections, licence/retrieval and coverage warning. Seek HHNK-authorized catchment/control aggregates; never convert absent Waterinfo to normal or safe.

findings.summary: The three-edge road graph omits internal access, crossings and destination acceptance.
findings.evidence: Only A7 north/south and N307 cross-boundary links exist. Hoorn/Hoorn Kersenboogerd rail and Dijklander access are context, while internal roads, waterfront access, live passability and emergency routing are absent.
findings.action: Retain NWB only for mobility/supply and non-additive semantics. Add critical destination/crossing state from official roads/rail feeds where available; otherwise show passability and acceptance Unknown.

findings.summary: Dijklander is represented as a point, not a first-72-hour dependency and acceptance state.
findings.evidence: RIVM and hospital sources establish a 24/7 SEH, acute obstetrics and serious-trauma transfer, but not live capacity, diversion, staff, backup utilities, oxygen, medicines or road/rail accessibility.
findings.action: Add authorized aggregate facility role, live acceptance/diversion, access, backup/fuel, critical supply and transfer status with valid time; all absent fields remain Unknown and the registered point never guarantees service.

findings.summary: Unsupported lake/defence dimensions are hidden behind derived-screening labels.
findings.evidence: Coastal reports unsupportedDimensions=[] while lacking named water body event, lake level/datum, wind setup, defence state and footprint. Exact local service and affected outputs remain visible.
findings.action: Populate unsupported dimensions and place the local limitation beside maps, briefs, announcements and exports. Preserve source/version/retrieval/validity/licence/coverage/NoData and keep context non-causal.

findings.summary: No auditable first-72-hour action/resource ledger represents Hoorn's documented authorities and dependencies.
findings.evidence: Hoorn documents notification and RWS/HHNK/municipality/safety-region roles, preparedness guidance and Dijklander; the model ingests no trigger, authority, assignment, resources, state or completion.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first records for high-water warning, outer-dike welfare/evacuation, defence/sewer action, road/rail control, hospital continuity/transfer, temporary water, reception, food/fuel/medicine, utility repairs and mutual aid.

findings.summary: The Hoorn BAG label point falls outside the generalized CBS boundary.
findings.evidence: The mandatory context gate reproduces one external label point while municipality identity, population and the other two place centres are coherent. Centroid/generalization and independent edition semantics can create this condition.
findings.action: Retain and disclose the mismatch; compare source-resolution BAG/CBS geometry before any correction and do not snap, discard or treat it as missing settlement population.

corrections.summary: Replace broad GM0405 coastal forcing with explicit Markermeer outer-dike and defence-event semantics.
corrections.validation: Without a selected named Markermeer/LIWO event, GM0405 direct flood is unsupported/Unknown and no precise direct affected count is shown; fixtures for NAP-scoped outer-dike and defence-breach scenarios reproduce footprint, timing, recession and NoData.

corrections.summary: Remove common neighbourhood ranking and ingest source-specific coastal/pluvial geometry.
corrections.validation: Unrelated presets no longer share the same top-five order; supported coastal fixtures prioritize the actual intersecting waterfront polygons and pluvial fixtures retain sewer-included flag and data coverage.

corrections.summary: Keep water/provider/grid/antenna/education/acute-care records context-only with strict Unknown semantics.
corrections.validation: Cards/exports show version, retrieval/valid time, licence, coverage and affectsSimulation=false; missing managers/capacities, empty drainage/observations and annual hospital fields never render as zero, safe, open or available.

corrections.summary: Represent Dijklander and Hoorn route access with authorized first-72-hour state.
corrections.validation: Hospital role, acceptance/diversion, transfer, critical utilities/supplies and A7/N307/rail/local access have time-stamped evidence or explicit Unknown and influence recovery only after a confirmed state/action.

corrections.summary: Implement a role-aware Unknown-first action and resource ledger for GM0405.
corrections.validation: At every checkpoint warning, outer-dike action, water/sewer decision, transport, hospital, reception/resupply and repair show authority, trigger, assignment, state, resource and source/valid time; absent facts remain Unknown.

residualLimitations: No reviewed public source provides complete safe-to-publish Liander/PWN/gas/telecom/drainage topology, current control state, backup endurance, crews, inventories or restoration estimates.
Markermeer flood impact depends on water level, wind setup, discharge operations, outer-dike geometry and defence condition; project and historic-event pages are not live forecasts.
HWH asset completeness varies; point geometry and registered capacity/status do not establish a functioning network or comparable throughput.
CBS/BAG/DUO/RIVM records omit visitors, harbour/recreation occupancy, commuters, home-care needs, live hospital load, shelters and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Current water, weather, road, warning and facility states may change after audit completion; stale or out-of-coverage data must degrade to Unknown.
provinceReviewFlags: Define province-wide IJsselmeer/Markermeer lake-flood semantics distinct from North Sea coastal surge and major-river flooding, with outer-dike versus defence-failure footprints.
Reconcile Hoorn, Waterland, Edam-Volendam, Koggenland, Medemblik and Enkhuizen dike/lake pathways using one versioned LIWO/RWS/HHNK evidence contract.
Test the repeated neighbourhood ranking defect across Noord-Holland coastal, polder, urban-pluvial and heat contexts.
Review BAG woonplaats label points against independently generalized municipal boundaries consistently; do not auto-snap coastal centroids.
Audit A7/N307/rail and Dijklander regional acute-care access/transfer dependencies without converting schedules or facilities into guaranteed availability.
Require Unknown-first 72-hour actions for outer-dike residents, hospital continuity, temporary water, evacuation/reception and household preparedness.
